460.t: His children, his son's grandfather Roy Gaines, and the Philippines
460.s: Laws talks about his daughter Ashley, who writes and sings, and his son Sky, whose grandfather is bluesman Roy Gaines. They end with a present from the Philippines.
460.q: Ashley. They call her Kristen. Some people call her Kristen. But I named her Ashley. She uses Kristen Cole – Kristen Ashley Cole. She’s very – she’s all over the place, like I told you, moving the hoop, the basketball hoop, earlier, an analogy. That’s the way she is in some ways. But she’s reliable…

460.s: Laws recalls the success of Family, with his arrangements and constant orders for the record.
460.q: That’s one, boy. That was another. Frankie Crocker in New York, he had it on high rotation, and it just – all over. That record did really – in fact, we still perform that. Just performed it in Manila.

460.t: The family ensemble, Debra's talent and Ronnie today
460.s: Laws recalls bringing family members into performances, Debra's gifts, and his view of Ronnie's gigging.
460.q: I did not have the family included in every situation, but whenever I could include them, I did. For instance, we played Carnegie Hall a couple times. We also did the Pavilion here. That’s when the Family LP came out, because Debra is pretty much – I always get her involved when there’s space for…

460.t: More about his son's tennis and spoiling children
460.s: Laws continues the tangent about training his son in tennis, a Bible saying about pampering children, and his son's present family circumstances.
460.q: wake him up to go – he had tennis matches to play. He was in a junior tournament. He won. Up to 14, he did real well, because we were out there practicing more than the average guy, plus he had the advantage of having his own court in the backyard. I found out later, though, you pamper them too…

383.s: Hinton asks Wilson's son Steven to join, and Steven mentions Woody Shaw and his interest in his father's trio work.
383.ch: Regional bands, politics and travel abroad
383.q: Oh, I just came back from New York to visit my mother. And she's out -- Woody Shaw was playing the Palace. And a very good bass player named Stafford James. Excellent. The drummer was excellent, too, (inaudible). I really enjoyed that. They played until 4:00 o'clock in the morning. Started at 10:00…

383.t: His five children and their music
383.s: Wilson gives a rundown of Theodore, Steven, Bill, James and Dune, their ages, schooling and musical talents, all with perfect pitch.
383.q: that marriage, a little girl, Dune, who's now 13 years old, D-u-n-e, and a brother James, who's 14 now. And he's named after my father, and my older brother, were both James. And also Joanne's son by her previous marriage with Bill Gidney is with us now and his name's William, we call him Bill. And…

383.t: Playing with his sons on television
383.s: Steven and Ted Jr. say they owe their playing to their father, who hired them, and Hinton calls Wilson exacting.
383.q: Well, for me, any ability I have to perform is exclusively because of Dad. It also gave me the ability to put together the jazz history courses, because I didn't even have to read about it because I heard it and saw it and could go back to it in retrospect. But the confidence in being a performer…

288.t: Playing the piano for pastime; his daughter
288.s: He says he sometimes banged piano and raised a daughter who is now in New Orleans.
288.ch: Society work, Camilla Todd and Storyville
288.q: Oh yeah. I used to like the piano. I used to kind of bang on that myself sometimes. Then sometimes I had to kind of help out. You really did. Maybe we could get a little

288.t: Whether the children of jazzmen carried on
288.s: He says most sons did not, citing Buddy Petit and Kid Rena.
288.q: Well, not a one that I knew, because all those that followed the step of their daddy, like I tell you, they went away. And first thing you know, like I say, through habits, you know, from the habits, they went away. Take like, for instance, Joe Petit's son, Buddy Petit. That guy, he was cut out to…

194.t: Cuba, brief boxing, and hopes for the future
194.s: He never went to Cuba, boxed briefly, and hopes to make his grandchildren happy.
194.q: I tried. You tried? Yeah. I boxed for about six months. Cause, I mean, I say boxed, but I mean I was just in the game because the first night I got whipped I quit, you know.

194.t: Crowded households and a sick singer
194.s: Longhair talks about his large family living together; Marquez mentions a household singer who is ill.
194.q: You know, see, you can treat you fair, but let you live, you know. You can make it. You just get a little something out of this, you know. Of course you have to get a little something out of this, I mean, you can live. And me, I got seven charons, at least I had seven, one time. And I got a bunch…

996.t: His daughters and the Beatles' enduring legacy
996.s: He talks about his daughters and grandchildren, and the lasting depth of Beatles scholarship.
996.q: Oh yeah. Both of my daughters are very hip. My youngest daughter is a successful songwriter. And she found her own path with it, when she was a teenager and beyond, we supported her, encouraged her. She knows the business. She knows how it works. And she’s been having hit records, not only as a…

996.s: His grandchildren aged seven and five are starting guitar and piano, while his guitars are adult-sized.
996.q: My eldest just started playing. My youngest just started piano lessons yesterday. Yeah, they’re seven and five so they’re still a little bit on the young side. Because my guitars, other than a ukulele or two, my guitars are kind of adult sized guitars.

215.t: Bucky's kids and the characters who visited the house
215.s: His son John's trio, and how the children met Zoot Sims, Joe Venuti and Slam Stewart at home.
215.q: Oh yeah. Yeah. They come up with some good stuff. Tunes — I know John is about to make an album. He does a lot of research on it. I used to tell him listen to this guy, listen to that guy. He does a great rendition of a certain tune you ought to look into. That’s all. That’s as far as it goes. But…

215.t: John Pizzarelli's career and playing with him at the Pierre
215.s: His son John plays seven-string, upcoming Smithsonian blue-guitar exhibition, John's influences, and their summer at the Pierre Hotel.
215.q: Yeah we’re going to — I haven’t played with him that much but when we do we do right into it. We can get that thing going right away. But we’re going to play at the Smithsonian in November. There’s an archtop exhibition going on, all the best guitar makers have made blue guitars.

61.t: His three children: a son who left engineering, daughters, the name Gregory
61.s: Son interned as an engineer and dropped it; daughter plays piano and wrote a rag; children's names.
61.q: Yeah, intern work for NYC, which he enjoyed greatly. He wanted to become a recording engineer and finally decided, no, he wasn’t going to, because he didn’t care too much working with some of the people that he would be working with. He liked rock and so forth, but he decided, no, this is not for…

61.t: His daughters take to riding and working with horses

61.q: All right. The harness horses is – I’m going to tell this story. My daughters loved riding horses, once they discovered that these horses that went past our house on Central Park West and into the park were stabled a block-and-a-half away, down 89th Street, the only stable in Manhattan. When they…

105.t: His children and his son Forest Hamilton's career

105.q: No. Fat Burgers. That was one of his products. He managed Isaac Hayes. He was responsible for Isaac getting an Academy Award. Watts Stax, you know, he did all that. He was in management. You know, he was a millionaire when he was 21. His first group was Love and by the time he was 21 years old,…

105.t: Advice on raising a teenage daughter
105.s: He advises Brown to become his daughter's friend, and says families that listen to jazz together stay together.
105.ch: Race, family and the younger generation
105.q: Oh, yeah. Man I have a lot of compassion for you people that have teenagers man, because the competition is so keen out there man, that you’ve got to -- you know, I don’t know how you can keep control over -- you know, it’s not a question of keeping control but, you know, I’ll hip you up to…

62.t: His son Anthony, grandson and Shuggie Otis
62.s: Wilson explains his grandson, Shuggie Otis's son by his daughter Terry, writes out his music, and his son Anthony tours with Diana Krall.

62.t: Grandson's school band and Lenny Kravitz
62.s: Wilson recalls the grandson's early guitar playing and school band with Lenny Kravitz.
62.q: He does, no, no, he does it by hand, does it by hand, does it by hand. He did all, the ones you talking about there, the one that we have now that, the new album that’s out. So I’m lucky that I got this grandson that is into it, my son is in, he can play and he started when he was like seven years…

589.t: His son Frayne as producer, and his children
589.s: Frayne produced eight or nine albums; none of his children became pianists, though Frayne and Kelly work in music.
589.q: That’s my son. He’s the producer on the one – Taking Another Look, yeah, that one. He’s produced eight or nine of my albums.

589.t: The Best of Ramsey Lewis cover and his seven children
589.s: Looking at an album cover, Lewis explains the Nehru jacket and identifies his seven children and grandchildren.
589.q: That was during a period – a very short period – that the Nehru jacket was popular. I don’t know why I chose to put on a Nehru jacket. Then I had on a white, fake, mock turtleneck. Yeah, it comes off very religious.

367.s: Young talks about his grandchildren, including a grandson who took his trumpet but does not play.
367.q: My grandchildren… my grandson, he doesn‘t play music, he wants to play so he got a trumpet. I gave him a trumpet. He jive at me like he‘s going to play. He ain‘t never going to play the trumpet, but he got my trumpet. I asked him to give me my trumpet back…

367.t: His three children and their music
367.s: Young names his daughter Judy, his late son Eugene Edward Young III and a younger daughter, and says his son became a horticulturist; Brown notes his own musician children.
367.q: Singers, oh that‘s great. My kids were musicians too, my daughter played the piano and, my son, he played, but, he played trumpet and… what else did he play… but he didn‘t turn out to be a musician for some reason. My son turned out to be a horticulture, whatever that is. He worked in all that kind…

80.t: His grandchildren and his children's cool reaction to his music
80.s: His grandson in Maryland is a young karate black belt with a trumpet; his own daughters were polite but unimpressed by his jazz fame.
80.ch: Postwar years, accident and lean times
80.q: Well, one of my grandsons told me, he's what, twelve, thirteen, now, and I'm not sure but what he still has found a -- and I gave him a trumpet, and I haven't seen Tony to talk to him in so doggone long, other than the telephone, because I've been in and out of the hospital, and they're down in…

80.t: Fats's second wife Anita and his pianist sons Maurice and Thomas Jr.
80.s: After jail Fats married Anita; his sons Maurice, Ronald and Junior play piano, and Maurice has turned from modern jazz to his father's style.
80.q: Oh, all those things. I mean you've heard of them. You will have anyway. And (when) he came out of jail, let me see, what did he do then? Well, naturally they separated, and he married his second wife, Anita. And then he had these -- Maurice and Ronald, two sons.

1.s: Milt and the Barkers talk about their grandson's music, Milt's daughter's piano lessons, and Sylvia, who writes poems and acts.
1.ch: Lu Barker and the Barbarin family
1.q: That's right. Exactly. And she writes poems and she writes songs, and she's interested in everything in the music. And she belongs to this big theatre there, you know, and then when comes here, right away she's going to the southern(?) theatre and all this... I mean, she loves that.

1.q: Well, she had two husbands. Her first husband was Rene Browner(?), and he passed away. She had one son for him, Larry Browner. And Larry has a little boy, Christopher, and now got one on the way.

614.t: His daughter Inge and grandchildren Tom and Alexandra

614.s: Before Detroit he stopped in Nashville, where his daughter plays bluegrass fiddle as a section musician and grandson Tom has returned to bluegrass.

But all the rest of them is, that's when they had a parade. I think a picture you snapped. We had a couple of Christian parade. I kiddin',…

246.q: Yeah, these runners, they're running. I'll be back. Listen, watch yourself, folks. I'm going to jump over there. I can see. Now, you take a walk now.

34.s: Burns's sister, children and grandsons played music.

185.ch: Home life and the father's death
185.q: Yeah, they're living in New Rochelle, New York. Up in New Rochelle. They rented their home out in Mount Vernon and then they moved to, that's the suburb like you know.

Robert Williams, Jr. Well, there's two of my boys, they're taking up this, uh, rock and roll. That, uh, beaters playing, uh, to keep it up, you see. So, uh, I think that's, uh,…

138.t: Brunies reunion visit at the Laine house and photos in the yard

968.s: His children took no interest in playing, though they love music.

But she never did take the name of Bolden. Hmm? She never did take the name of Bolden. She never once married.…

800.q: He plays around. He plays around a little around California. He plays a little around California.

918.s: Lala family trumpeters and Parenti's nephew, a drummer.

When I was living on the Jantilly Street, I had this boy on clarinet, the next boy on drum, and the girl on the violin. So when I moved from Jantilly Street and moved back here, they just put it…

635.q: See, this is the one named after me, George. He's the bad brother. George is Norman and Junior is Henry. Oh, yeah. That's great. That's great.

We was trying to get a band together for King Floyd and he came auditioned for me and told me he was considering this boy. I…

830.t: Charlotte's family and the three Georges
830.s: Charlotte's son lives in California; they sort out George I, II and III, a grandson in the reserve band holding his grandfather's last cornet.
830.q: She's six years and seven months older than him. I don't know if you say stuff. She's six years and seven months older than him. He was just four years old when his daddy died. Ernest. Bring the father back to daddy.

690.s: Pope's four daughters sang in New York and Canada; he has no band photographs.
690.q: Thank you. You have a picture of me all. You know, they... I had four daughters. They sang in New York, you know. Stayed there quite a while. Until one died, I broke up the key. Really? Yes. They gave them pretty well. Mm-hmm. They stayed there quite a while. They went to Canada and stayed there…

Yeah, Sam told me that, Sam Majaudi. Yeah, he died. Yeah. I played last year, a year or two ago with the police band. What,…

780.t: Why he will not return to music; his children
780.s: He sees returning as a waste of time and cannot afford it; he has two children and a daughter getting married.
780.q: Well, no. I think it would be just a waste of time, a big waste of time. I don't think there would be any point in trying to go back into it. Well, I guess the sound had changed, but that wouldn't mean anything. I think I can handle myself well enough to change too. But I wouldn't want to get back…

196.t: His daughter's music; never played with string bands
196.s: His daughter is a union musician; he has three children. He never played with string bands like Doc Souchon's.
196.ch: After the music: Army, public service, family
196.q: She's in the union. My daughter's in the union. She's accomplished. She's very good. She plays wonderfully. She's married. I have three children. They live up in Metairick.

905.t: Phillips' family musicians and Ricard changing to bass
905.s: His son plays bass, grandson drums; talk of bass amplifiers and Ricard Alexis switching from trumpet.
905.q: I got a boy playing drums, but I don't know why he has. Oh, is that right? He's been away from here. When he left here, he was playing drums.

559.t: His daughters' view of his profession

And I didn’t have the — I didn’t want to discourage her because this is a tough business. I’m not kidding, this is a…

616.s: His stepson Cary and son Thad did not pursue music after seeing his struggles.

795.t: His children and the Emmy nomination

Okay I’ll give you an example about him. At two years old…

But he never stopped singing. So now, he came back to me and he says, “I want to sing.” I says okay. Come to find…

593.q: Oh the sixth is new, she’s a year old, Ruby. And her mother is a pianist and piano teacher and composer. I don’t think she named her after Thelonious Monk’s “Ruby My Dear” although she knows the music. Yeah that’s the newest one.

792.t: Son Duffy and his drumming, and daughters

But jazz is such a personal thing that the thing about jazz, there’s a whole lot of people want to play a certain…

502.t: Nature in his writing and his children's music
